summary: Green's Point at Letete, New Brunswick: a fog alarm from 1879, a lighthouse from 1903, the light inactive since 1999 while the fog signal still sounds; run by a local association.

corrections.why: 1879 is the steam fog alarm. The lighthouse was first put in operation on 1 September 1903 (Marine 1903 report). Event 1879 should be fog_signal_installed.
Light decommissioned 8 September 1999 (LF); Rowlett: inactive since 1999, fog signal active. Coast Guard list has no light at this site, only the fog signal (list 71, H4120).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The light has been inactive since 1999 (LF: decommissioned 8 September 1999; Rowlett). The fog signal remains active (LF; Rowlett; Coast Guard list). The record's 'active' applies to the fog signal only.
1879 is the steam fog alarm (LF; Rowlett 'fog signal station established 1879'). The lighthouse dates from 1903 (Marine 1903 report). The record's 1879 'established' date reflects the fog station.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: LighthouseFriends (the main narrative, which cites Department reports), three Marine reports with primary wording, Rowlett, and the Coast Guard list. Keeper roster from LighthouseFriends; the Marine keeper lists corroborate George Helms and Sydney Dines only loosely (OCR). The 1907 keeper list also reads 'Dines, Chas. H Letite Light' (OCR), a second Dines not in LighthouseFriends; not used, to be checked against the page image. Sydney's name is OCR 'Svdney' in the 1907 list. Matched by OCR position. The Saxby Gale (October 1869) predates the station (fog alarm 1878-79); LighthouseFriends and mynewbrunswick.ca place it in the station's narrative as cutting off the point. Not used. The 1921 Marine report's New Brunswick block lists 'Erection of new fog-alarm building, the steam plant replaced by oil engines and Class B diaphone'; the OCR does not tie it to Letete by name, so the 1920-21 works rest on LighthouseFriends. Chronicling America 'Letete' search returned only unrelated OCR hits; no newspaper used. 'Velda Dandall' is LighthouseFriends' spelling and may be a misprint. Keepers from 1963 to 1996 are named only as LighthouseFriends prints them, in public role. Distances: the 1903 Marine report says '12 miles'; the story reads it as nautical miles, as the guide asks for sea ranges. The mynewbrunswick.ca and Wikipedia texts repeat LighthouseFriends and are not cited. Head Harbour is on the map (ca-nb-head-harbour) and is used in other_stations. The Coast Guard list's lack of a light at Letete is the basis for the record's Fl R 6s being stale; this is noted, not corrected, because a human should confirm before changing the characteristic. Fact-check 2026-10-28: all 51 evidence quotes were found on the first run. Story changes: 'on the charts' moved from the 1903 report to LighthouseFriends (the report says only 'Mascabin point'); the nautical-mile conversion of the blast range removed (LighthouseFriends gives six miles); the 1903 range stays 'twelve miles' as printed, not stated as nautical; 'presented locally' and 'sent him a medal' changed to what LighthouseFriends prints; the 1937 electricity date attributed to Prescott's recollection as LighthouseFriends gives it; fiscal years given (the 1907 report covers the nine months to 31 March 1907); 'the Coast Guard list has no light' changed to what the list shows (an entry for the fog signal only). Image check: the 1907 keeper-list row (archive scan p.149, printed p.142) was viewed in the archive viewer, but the first name could not be resolved at that resolution; the archive OCR reads 'Svdney'. The story therefore says only 'a Dines'. A second entry on that list, 'Dines, Chas. H Letite Light', is not used. A Marine report in the corpus under identifier 1921v57i7p21_1575 (scan p.95) names 'Letite passage' for a new fog-alarm building and oil-engine diaphone; it could support the 1920 works if a human approves adding it.
